clue.text: Feverish girl with nervous twitch

parts.note: Fran is a girl's name, short for Frances
a tic is an involuntary nervous twitch

explanation.surface: A girl with a nervous twitch seems feverish and agitated.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe wild, agitated excitement, so they are synonyms in the sense of being worked up.

clue.text: Force the Queen to release fanatic

parts.note: F is the physics symbol for force
ER, Elizabeth Regina, stands for the Queen
to vent is to release or let out

explanation.surface: Making the Queen free a zealot.
explanation.definitionFit: A fervent supporter is passionately zealous, which is what fanatic describes as an adjective.

clue.text: One hopes you're entering these pleas?

definitions.meaning: the solver of this puzzle is hoped to be filling the grid with correct solutions
a plea is a defendant's formal reply to a charge in court

explanation.walkthrough: The first reading is self-referential: it addresses you, the solver, writing in the grid.
explanation.definitionFit: Solvers fill in replies to clues, and in court a plea is the formal reply to a charge.

clue.text: Reveal youngster's opening the box

parts.note: to tell is to reveal

indicators.note: an opening is the first letter of the word youngster

explanation.surface: A youngster unwrapping a present reveals what is in the box.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the box' is British slang for television.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are informal British words for a television set.

clue.text: Doctor cures most clients

indicators.note: to doctor something is to tamper with it, so these letters are reordered

explanation.surface: A doctor heals most of the patients on the books.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctor' reads as a noun but is a verb meaning tamper with.
explanation.definitionFit: Clients and shoppers are both people who buy goods or services from a business.

clue.text: Boring unruly adolescent with debts?

parts.note: a Ted, or Teddy boy, was a rowdy 1950s British youth
IOUs are written promises to pay, hence debts

explanation.surface: A dull, troublesome teenager who also owes money.
explanation.walkthrough: A Teddy boy (Ted) was a 1950s British youth subculture known for drape jackets and rowdiness.
explanation.definitionFit: Something boring is dull and wearisome, a direct synonym of the adjective in the answer.

clue.text: Cross yard following inspection

indicators.note: following places the letter for yard after the inspection word

parts.note: a test is an examination or inspection

explanation.surface: A yard was crossed following an inspection.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cross' reads as a verb, but it is the adjective meaning angry.
explanation.definitionFit: Being cross is being irritable and short-tempered, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Showed heads of department increasing shamelessness and messed around

indicators.note: heads of means the first letter of each of the next three words

parts.note: to play is to mess around

explanation.surface: Department heads grew ever more shameless and fooled about.
explanation.definitionFit: To display something is to put it on show, so a past-tense synonym.

clue.text: Aspiration to leave hospital and be worthy of work

indicators.note: to leave means the letter for hospital is taken out

parts.note: a hope is an aspiration
to rate is to deserve, as in 'rates a mention'

explanation.surface: Someone hopes to be discharged and to earn their keep.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Aspiration' also means a breathed H sound, a tempting false lead toward dropping H.
explanation.definitionFit: A machine that works is said to operate, so the two verbs share the function sense.

clue.text: Partly fasten it askew, lifting material

indicators.note: in a down clue, lifting means the letters are read upwards, so backwards
partly means only part of these words is used, a run of letters inside them

explanation.surface: Fastening something crooked while picking up some cloth.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a thin satin-like fabric, so it is an example of material.

clue.text: Thieves oddly set to be restrained by court orders

indicators.note: being restrained by something means being held within it, so these letters go inside

parts.note: rules are orders issued by a court

indicators.note: oddly means take the odd-numbered letters, first and third, of the word set

explanation.surface: Thieves look likely to be held in check by injunctions from a judge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Thieves' is a verb here, not a plural noun.
explanation.definitionFit: To rustle is to steal livestock, so someone who rustles thieves cattle or horses.

clue.text: Dubious cult trapping American quietly

indicators.note: trapping means the cult word holds the other letters inside it

parts.note: a cult is a religious sect
p (piano) is the musical marking for quietly

explanation.surface: A shady cult that has caught an American who kept quiet.
explanation.definitionFit: Something dubious is open to doubt, which is what a suspect claim or alibi is.

clue.text: Each person's so stiff after end of exercise

indicators.note: after places the following pieces behind the letter from exercise
the end of a word is its final letter, here of exercise

parts.note: so means very, as in 'so tired'
a stiff is slang for a dead body

explanation.surface: Everyone ends up aching and stiff after a workout.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stiff' looks like an adjective about sore muscles, but it is the noun for a corpse. The 's of the definition is read as 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Each person, taken all together, means all people collectively, the everyone-pronoun.

clue.text: Master and student get paid

parts.note: L is for learner, as on a learner driver's plate
to earn is to get paid for work

explanation.surface: A master and a student both get paid.
explanation.walkthrough: L comes from the L-plates that British learner drivers display.
explanation.definitionFit: To master a skill is to acquire it fully, which is what learning it means.

clue.text: Tense requests for jobs

parts.note: T is the grammatical abbreviation for tense
asks are requests, as in 'big asks'

explanation.surface: Nervous requests for work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tense' reads as an adjective (anxious) but supplies the grammar abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Jobs and chores are pieces of work to be done, the same as assignments.

clue.text: Results so-so until reforms

indicators.note: reforms means forms again, so these letters are put in a new order

explanation.surface: Mediocre outcomes persist until changes are made.
explanation.definitionFit: Solutions are the outcomes of working out problems, so they are results or answers.

clue.text: Spinning Jenny, to me, is fun

indicators.note: spinning turns things round and round, so these letters are mixed into a new order

explanation.surface: A speaker says operating a spinning jenny is great fun.
explanation.walkthrough: A spinning jenny is an early multi-spindle spinning machine, which makes 'Spinning' look like part of a name.
explanation.definitionFit: Fun is pleasure or amusement, the same as delight taken in something.

clue.text: After day in prison, European intended to ignore a verdict

indicators.note: in means the letter for day goes inside the word for prison

parts.note: jug is slang for prison

indicators.note: to ignore means to leave out the letter named

parts.note: meant means intended

explanation.surface: After a day in jail, a European meant to disregard the jury's decision.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After' is a link word joining the opening picture to the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: A verdict is the decision of a court, which is what a judgment from the bench is.

clue.text: Educated Conservative is livid, unfortunately, about Spain

indicators.note: about means the scrambled letters go around the letter for Spain
unfortunately suggests things gone wrong, so the letters of 'is livid' are scrambled

parts.note: E is the international vehicle code for Spain (España)

explanation.surface: A cultured Tory is furious about something concerning Spain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unfortunately' turns IS LIVID into IVILISD, and 'about' wraps that round E so that it becomes IVILISED.
explanation.definitionFit: A civilised person is cultivated and refined, which is what being educated suggests.

clue.text: Embarrassed after chap's plastered

indicators.note: after places the colour word behind the word for chap

parts.note: a cove is old British slang for a chap
an embarrassed person goes red

explanation.surface: A man is ashamed after getting drunk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plastered' wants to mean drunk; it means coated, as a wall is plastered.
explanation.definitionFit: A surface plastered with posters is coated or spread over with them.

clue.text: Absurd to change leader — that's plain to see

indicators.note: changing the leader means swapping the first letter of the word for another

parts.note: risible means laughable, absurd

explanation.surface: It is obviously ridiculous to replace the boss.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue does not say what the new first letter is; only V turns the word into a real one meaning evident.
explanation.definitionFit: Something visible can be seen, so it is plain to see or evident.

clue.text: Sleazy nightclub limiting Romeo's enthusiasm

indicators.note: limiting means enclosing on both sides, so one piece holds the other

parts.note: a dive is a seedy bar or club
Romeo is the radio code word for R

explanation.surface: A seedy club keeps in check a romantic man's eagerness.
explanation.definitionFit: Drive is energy and determination, the same as zeal or enthusiasm for getting on.

clue.text: Assume one quarry contains silver

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: contains means the quarry word holds the silver symbol

parts.note: a mine is a quarry or pit
Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

explanation.surface: Suppose a quarry holds silver ore.
explanation.definitionFit: To imagine can mean to suppose or presume, as in 'I imagine she's right'.

clue.text: Makes bigger offers

definitions.meaning: holds out or proffers, as in giving a welcome or credit

explanation.definitionFit: The verb means both to enlarge something and to proffer it, as a hand or an invitation.

clue.text: Call on model after six

indicators.note: after places the model's word behind the numeral

parts.note: VI is six in Roman numerals
to sit is to model for an artist

explanation.surface: Visit a fashion model once it is past six o'clock.
explanation.definitionFit: To call on someone is to drop in at their home, a phrasal synonym.

clue.text: Meal turning bakers fat

indicators.note: turning means changing form, so the letters of these words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A meal that is making bakers overweight.
explanation.definitionFit: The first meal of the day is a specific example of a meal.

clue.text: Corrupt Democrat located

parts.note: base means morally low, corrupt

explanation.surface: A crooked politician has been tracked down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Corrupt' looks like an anagram signal, but it is the adjective base.
explanation.definitionFit: To be located somewhere is to be situated or stationed there.

clue.text: Noted family heartlessly wrapping the present

indicators.note: wrapping means the remaining letters go round the other piece
heartlessly means the middle letter of the word is removed

parts.note: kin is one's family
now is the present time

explanation.surface: A well-known family coldly giftwraps a present.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the present' looks like a gift, but it means the current moment.
explanation.definitionFit: Something noted is well known or famous, so the adjectives share that sense.

clue.text: Strips bones, eating most of another

indicators.note: eating means the first piece takes the other inside it

parts.note: ribs are bones

indicators.note: most of a word means it loses its final letter

parts.note: another bone, as the clue has just mentioned bones

explanation.surface: Someone stripping meat off bones while chewing on yet another.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strips' looks like a verb but is the plural noun.
explanation.definitionFit: Ribbons are long narrow strips, of cloth or of anything torn to shreds.

clue.text: Greek god with one leg wasting away

parts.note: Eros is the Greek god of love
I is the Roman numeral for one
on is the leg side in cricket

explanation.surface: A one-legged Greek god is wasting away.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the leg side of the field is also called the on side.
explanation.definitionFit: Erosion is the gradual wearing away of something, as rock is worn by water.

clue.text: Daughter, rejecting most of pudding, got up

indicators.note: rejecting means sending back, so the shortened word is turned backwards
most of means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: pudding is the British word for dessert

explanation.surface: A daughter turned down most of her pudding and left the table.
explanation.walkthrough: 'got up' here means dressed up in clothes, not risen from bed.
explanation.definitionFit: Got up can mean attired, as in 'got up in fancy clothes', so it means clothed.

clue.text: Flipping crazy golfer's after new holes

indicators.note: after places the golfer's name behind the letter for new
flipping turns something over, so this word is read backwards

parts.note: a nut is a crazy person
Ernie Els is a South African golfer

explanation.surface: An exasperated player says the mad golfer is after new holes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flipping' reads as a mild British curse but signals the reversal.
explanation.definitionFit: Tunnels are passages dug underground, so they are holes or burrows.
